description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtRescate’s proposed response aligns with the 1st SA 2025 strategy SHF Envelop 12 by emphasizing integrated, multi-sectoral interventions that address urgent humanitarian needs while enhancing long-term community resilience. Prior to proposal submission, Rescate coordinated with relevant clusters, partners, HAC DINGO, ensuring technical harmonization of the proposed activities.ltbrgtDuring the planning phase, Rescate engaged with sectoral focal points, active partners local communities to ensure interventions align with sectoral priorities respond to evidence-based needs.ltbrgtShelter ltbrgtRescate is finishing shelter rehab under the 1st SA 2024 continues in 2025 to focus on sub-districts prioritized under the 1st SA 2025 with a severity score of 4. These areas remain underserved following the return of IDPs refugees, particularly regarding the rehab of damaged housing adjacent sewage pipelines.ltbrgtIn DEZ following the successful rehab of water sanitation networks, Rescate implemented a CFW Solid Waste Debris Management project. In Hameidiyyeh, community members have requested additional shelter, 50 Houses WASH. In Aleppo, the community reached to Rescate with the mayor pledge for support in rehab 50 houses. A similar approach was taken in RDam Yelda, where communities bordering the current closing shelter project requested continued support with additional 120 houses. ltbrgtThe proposed intervention addresses the needs based on damage assessments HHs vulnerability, aiming to restore safety, privacy, and dignity. It also contributes to the protection and reintegration of returnees particularly women children by enhancing their access to safe, habitable environments, in line with shelter priorities.ltbrgtWASH ltbrgtIn the three areas addressed with shelter, communities requested sewage rehabilitation to mitigate environmental degradation prevent serious health risks, most notably the spread of leishmaniasis which continues to threaten public health due to insufficient waste water management.ltbrgtWASH improvement is essential not only for health protection but also for reducing the risk of waterborne vector-borne diseases in vulnerable returnee communities. 4,000 beneficiaries will benefit from this activity. These efforts will significantly reduce health risks contribute to the overall resilience of communities recovering from conflict and displacement.ltbrgtFSS- Livelihoods ltbrgtUnder FSS Strategic Priority 2 to build resilience among populations affected by conflict, displacement, economic shocks especially drought, Rescate will strengthen local food production systems in Dara 200 Tirbet Azaz 453 through the provision of fodder to support breeders, addressing the lack of pastures productivity.ltbrgtThe project is designed not only to support livestock restore HHs income streams but also to increase the resilience of FHHs women laborers, who form most of the agricultural livestock workforce in Syria. By ensuring access to fodder inputs, Rescate supports women’s roles in sustaining HHs economies enhances their protection by reducing the need for risky coping mechanisms, such as asset depletion or unsafe labor migration.ltbrgtIn Daret Azza Busra Al Sham, Daraa, Rescate will provide fodder to 453 200 breeders, respectively. This complement previous FSS efforts responds to community's needs, including rehab the Grain Center bolster resilience creates sustainable livelihood for local communities.ltbrgtRescate’s proposed response is guided by principles of community ownership, resilience-building gender-sensitive protection. Special attention given to ensure interventions benefit women girls, who are often disproportionately affected by economic instability protection threats. The proposal also prioritizes sustainability by supporting infrastructure livelihoods critical to long-term recovery.ltbrgtlt/pgt
